‍4) Privacy Is the Priority:
There are no required social events. Our priority is providing privacy, a quiet environment, and security for all our guests. We won’t invest in luxury buildings like hotels or event spaces. We rent existing empty apartments and townhouses from the owners, put IKEA-type furniture in, and list the clean rooms on multiple digital platforms. We grow by our operational profit base, which comes from guests being charged fair prices and the revenue owners receive. However, what drives our growth is not the number of rooms, but our deep understanding of how to care for guests and rooms 24/7, and the intangible value within them.

CrossOver’s goal is to help our guests achieve their goals and dreams by providing the most affordable and flexible housing environment available. But it doesn’t stop here. host_about:
Dear Airbnb guests!

Thanks for checking my profile. I manage furnished monthly rentals and co-living spaces in Manhattan, Queens, and Brooklyn with my team members. I have been managing furnished apartments for a decade and have had more than 5,600 guests from 90 countries so far. Please feel free to ask me any questions or requests!

*I can speak Japanese as well! Please feel free to contact me in Japanese.

Who we are: Our Principles

1) Growing Our Alumni Community:
We don’t require any extra/hidden fees to maximize our profits. Instead, our focus is on growing our alumni community. We believe that our services and fair pricing speak for themselves among our guests. Our alumni posted 700+ reviews from 2019 to 2021. What’s more, 80% of the reviews gave us five stars and 97% awarded more than four stars. Our alumni community spans the globe with 87 unique nationalities, and it has been expanding. We look forward to serving all our new guests: our alumni of tomorrow.
‍

‍2) Transparency. One All-Inclusive Price. That’s What We’re About:
There’s no math required. The price for our one-month minimum stay is simple and fair, no matter how long you stay with us. Our one-month price is already competitive (averaging $1,200 to $2,200, with 80% of our 150 rooms under $1,900 per month), compared to others’ discounted prices for three- to six-month stays. In 2020, 50%+ of our customers extended their original stay by a few months. There’s really no substitute for all-inclusive furnished rentals and a co-living environment, with a furnished private room, that’s ready for you on day one.
‍

‍3) Increasing Value for the Local Property Industry:
We provide co-living communities for our guests by helping property owners draw more value from under-managed residential properties. We care about our customer community, of course, but we’re also excited about uniting property owners, vendors, and our team on one digital platform.
‍

‍4) Privacy Is the Priority:
There are no required social events. Our priority is providing privacy, a quiet environment, and security for all our guests. Our team will take care of cleaning the common spaces every week, so that our kitchen/dining areas are always comfortable. But if you want to expand your network or social circle, our office at WeWork offers you day/after-work communities. We just moved our headquarters to the newest WeWork offices in Long Island City, which is easily accessible by all subway lines.


‍5) 10 Years Perfecting the Co-Living Mindset:
Our founder started this business in his apartment after he couldn’t find appropriately priced accommodation for his first three months in New York. But our whole team has experienced co-living firsthand, so we understand what the customer feels and will need next. “We live and breathe co-living: first as roommates, and now serving our co-living guests.”
‍

‍6) A Sustainable Business Model in the Sharing Economy:
We won’t invest in luxury buildings like hotels or event spaces. We rent existing empty apartments and townhouses from the owners, put IKEA-type furniture in, and list the clean rooms on multiple digital platforms. We grow by our operational profit base, which comes from guests being charged fair prices and the revenue owners receive. However, what drives our growth is not the number of rooms, but our deep understanding of how to care for guests and rooms 24/7, and the intangible value within them.
‍

‍7) Our Vision - Making Dreams Come True:
CrossOver’s goal is to help our guests achieve their goals and dreams by providing the most affordable and flexible housing environment available. But it doesn’t stop here. Our guests’ dreams are expanding to a variety of locations around the globe, and CrossOver will be right there with them—powering the dreams of residents, landlords, and our staff in the wider world.

host_about:
Dear Airbnb guests!

Thanks for checking my profile. I manage furnished monthly rentals and co-living spaces in Manhattan, Queens, and Brooklyn with my team members. I have been managing furnished apartments for a decade and have had more than 5,600 guests from 90 countries so far. Please feel free to ask me any questions or requests!

*I can speak Japanese as well! Please feel free to contact me in Japanese.

Who we are: Our Principles

1) Growing Our Alumni Community:
We don’t require any extra/hidden fees to maximize our profits. Instead, our focus is on growing our alumni community. We believe that our services and fair pricing speak for themselves among our guests. Our alumni posted 700+ reviews from 2019 to 2021. What’s more, 80% of the reviews gave us five stars and 97% awarded more than four stars. Our alumni community spans the globe with 87 unique nationalities, and it has been expanding. We look forward to serving all our new guests: our alumni of tomorrow.
‍

‍2) Transparency. One All-Inclusive Price. That’s What We’re About:
There’s no math required. The price for our one-month minimum stay is simple and fair, no matter how long you stay with us. Our one-month price is already competitive (averaging $1,200 to $2,200, with 80% of our 150 rooms under $1,900 per month), compared to others’ discounted prices for three- to six-month stays. In 2020, 50%+ of our customers extended their original stay by a few months. There’s really no substitute for all-inclusive furnished rentals and a co-living environment, with a furnished private room, that’s ready for you on day one.
‍

‍3) Increasing Value for the Local Property Industry:
We provide co-living communities for our guests by helping property owners draw more value from under-managed residential properties. We care about our customer community, of course, but we’re also excited about uniting property owners, vendors, and our team on one digital platform.
‍

‍4) Privacy Is the Priority:
There are no required social events. Our priority is providing privacy, a quiet environment, and security for all our guests. Our team will take care of cleaning the common spaces every week, so that our kitchen/dining areas are always comfortable. But if you want to expand your network or social circle, our office at WeWork offers you day/after-work communities. We just moved our headquarters to the newest WeWork offices in Long Island City, which is easily accessible by all subway lines.


‍5) 10 Years Perfecting the Co-Living Mindset:
Our founder started this business in his apartment after he couldn’t find appropriately priced accommodation for his first three months in New York. But our whole team has experienced co-living firsthand, so we understand what the customer feels and will need next. “We live and breathe co-living: first as roommates, and now serving our co-living guests.”
‍

‍6) A Sustainable Business Model in the Sharing Economy:
We won’t invest in luxury buildings like hotels or event spaces. We rent existing empty apartments and townhouses from the owners, put IKEA-type furniture in, and list the clean rooms on multiple digital platforms. We grow by our operational profit base, which comes from guests being charged fair prices and the revenue owners receive. However, what drives our growth is not the number of rooms, but our deep understanding of how to care for guests and rooms 24/7, and the intangible value within them.

host_about:
Each suite is designed and curated with the guest in mind.

I am not a typical host, I like learning and getting to know my guests on a personal level, before you request to book with me please be comfortable answering the following…

I have been hosting for 15 years and felt airbnb becoming transactional and impersonal.  In an effort to host from the heart, I take a personal approach to hosting. Even more so when many guests have told me hosts haven’t  asked them a questions in 10 years, what a missed opportunity to connect with humanity. 

To me Airbnb is about community, specifically my community. I hope when visitors stay with me they feel like it’s  an extension of their homes. 

I like to get to know and learn about my guests and about me in return. There is an incredible opportunity for human connection. Do you mind if I ask you some questions? But before I do, I would like you to get to know me. 

I’m a born and bred New Yorker, who is fascinated by people, naturally I became a behavioral scientist and researcher. More than that I am also a mom to a wonderful 6 year old son. I adore arts and antiques and have a penchant for designing and decorating beautiful inspiring spaces. My goal is to create a warm and cozy environment where guests are intrigued and commune with the decor and experience the space. When they arrive I want them to touch every time and  provoke wonder and conversations. 

If you don’t mind please tell me about yourself? Where are you from originally? Did you grow up in there?

What do you do for fun?  Actually what does fun mean to you, what are your hobbies, what book are your currently reading, ( I’m reading How Emotions Are Made: The Secret Life of the Brain by Lisa Feldman Barrett).

What is your favorite cuisine? I could eat Thai, Mexican and Italian every day and never get bored, my comfort food is Haitian. Fun to me means being in the moment, experiencing life second by second, despite whatever worries I are occurring around me.  Also it’s  fun to visit old homes and emerge myself in museums, I love live music and love plays and musicals. My hobbies are real estate prospecting, antiquing and interior decorating. I look forward to learning about you .

Dear Airbnb guests!

Thanks for checking my profile. I manage furnished monthly rentals and co-living spaces in Manhattan, Queens, and Brooklyn with my team members. I have been managing furnished apartments for a decade and have had more than 5,600 guests from 90 countries so far. Please feel free to ask me any questions or requests!

*I can speak Japanese as well! Please feel free to contact me in Japanese.

Who we are: Our Principles

1) Growing Our Alumni Community:
We don’t require any extra/hidden fees to maximize our profits. Instead, our focus is on growing our alumni community. We believe that our services and fair pricing speak for themselves among our guests. Our alumni posted 700+ reviews from 2019 to 2021. What’s more, 80% of the reviews gave us five stars and 97% awarded more than four stars. Our alumni community spans the globe with 87 unique nationalities, and it has been expanding. We look forward to serving all our new guests: our alumni of tomorrow.
‍

‍2) Transparency. One All-Inclusive Price. That’s What We’re About:
There’s no math required. The price for our one-month minimum stay is simple and fair, no matter how long you stay with us. Our one-month price is already competitive (averaging $1,200 to $2,200, with 80% of our 150 rooms under $1,900 per month), compared to others’ discounted prices for three- to six-month stays. In 2020, 50%+ of our customers extended their original stay by a few months. There’s really no substitute for all-inclusive furnished rentals and a co-living environment, with a furnished private room, that’s ready for you on day one.
‍

‍3) Increasing Value for the Local Property Industry:
We provide co-living communities for our guests by helping property owners draw more value from under-managed residential properties. We care about our customer community, of course, but we’re also excited about uniting property owners, vendors, and our team on one digital platform.
‍

‍4) Privacy Is the Priority:
There are no required social events. Our priority is providing privacy, a quiet environment, and security for all our guests. Our team will take care of cleaning the common spaces every week, so that our kitchen/dining areas are always comfortable. But if you want to expand your network or social circle, our office at WeWork offers you day/after-work communities. We just moved our headquarters to the newest WeWork offices in Long Island City, which is easily accessible by all subway lines.


‍5) 10 Years Perfecting the Co-Living Mindset:
Our founder started this business in his apartment after he couldn’t find appropriately priced accommodation for his first three months in New York. But our whole team has experienced co-living firsthand, so we understand what the customer feels and will need next. “We live and breathe co-living: first as roommates, and now serving our co-living guests.”

Dear Airbnb guests!

Thanks for checking my profile. I manage furnished monthly rentals and co-living spaces in Manhattan, Queens, and Brooklyn with my team members. I have been managing furnished apartments for a decade and have had more than 5,600 guests from 90 countries so far. Please feel free to ask me any questions or requests!

Who we are: Our Principles

1) Growing Our Alumni Community:
We don’t require any extra/hidden fees to maximize our profits. Instead, our focus is on growing our alumni community. We believe that our services and fair pricing speak for themselves among our guests. Our alumni posted 700+ reviews from 2019 to 2021. What’s more, 80% of the reviews gave us five stars and 97% awarded more than four stars. Our alumni community spans the globe with 87 unique nationalities, and it has been expanding. We look forward to serving all our new guests: our alumni of tomorrow.
‍

‍2) Transparency. One All-Inclusive Price. That’s What We’re About:
There’s no math required. The price for our one-month minimum stay is simple and fair, no matter how long you stay with us. Our one-month price is already competitive (averaging $1,200 to $2,200, with 80% of our 150 rooms under $1,900 per month), compared to others’ discounted prices for three- to six-month stays. In 2020, 50%+ of our customers extended their original stay by a few months. There’s really no substitute for all-inclusive furnished rentals and a co-living environment, with a furnished private room, that’s ready for you on day one.
‍

‍3) Increasing Value for the Local Property Industry:
We provide co-living communities for our guests by helping property owners draw more value from under-managed residential properties. We care about our customer community, of course, but we’re also excited about uniting property owners, vendors, and our team on one digital platform.
‍

‍4) Privacy Is the Priority:
There are no required social events. Our priority is providing privacy, a quiet environment, and security for all our guests. Our team will take care of cleaning the common spaces every week, so that our kitchen/dining areas are always comfortable. But if you want to expand your network or social circle, our office at WeWork offers you day/after-work communities. We just moved our headquarters to the newest WeWork offices in Long Island City, which is easily accessible by all subway lines.


‍5) 10 Years Perfecting the Co-Living Mindset:
Our founder started this business in his apartment after he couldn’t find appropriately priced accommodation for his first three months in New York. But our whole team has experienced co-living firsthand, so we understand what the customer feels and will need next. “We live and breathe co-living: first as roommates, and now serving our co-living guests.”
‍

‍6) A Sustainable Business Model in the Sharing Economy:
We won’t invest in luxury buildings like hotels or event spaces. We rent existing empty apartments and townhouses from the owners, put IKEA-type furniture in, and list the clean rooms on multiple digital platforms. We grow by our operational profit base, which comes from guests being charged fair prices and the revenue owners receive. However, what drives our growth is not the number of rooms, but our deep understanding of how to care for guests and rooms 24/7, and the intangible value within them.
‍

‍7) Our Vision - Making Dreams Come True:
CrossOver’s goal is to help our guests achieve their goals and dreams by providing the most affordable and flexible housing environment available. But it doesn’t stop here. Our guests’ dreams are expanding to a variety of locations around the globe, and CrossOver will be right there with them—powering the dreams of residents, landlords, and our staff in the wider world.

host_about:
Dear Airbnb guests!

Thanks for checking my profile. I manage furnished monthly rentals and co-living spaces in Manhattan, Queens, and Brooklyn with my team members. I have been managing furnished apartments for a decade and have had more than 5,600 guests from 90 countries so far. Please feel free to ask me any questions or requests!

*I can speak Japanese as well! Please feel free to contact me in Japanese.

Who we are: Our Principles

1) Growing Our Alumni Community:
We don’t require any extra/hidden fees to maximize our profits. Instead, our focus is on growing our alumni community. We believe that our services and fair pricing speak for themselves among our guests. Our alumni posted 700+ reviews from 2019 to 2021. What’s more, 80% of the reviews gave us five stars and 97% awarded more than four stars. Our alumni community spans the globe with 87 unique nationalities, and it has been expanding. We look forward to serving all our new guests: our alumni of tomorrow.
‍

‍2) Transparency. One All-Inclusive Price. That’s What We’re About:
There’s no math required. The price for our one-month minimum stay is simple and fair, no matter how long you stay with us. Our one-month price is already competitive (averaging $1,200 to $2,200, with 80% of our 150 rooms under $1,900 per month), compared to others’ discounted prices for three- to six-month stays. In 2020, 50%+ of our customers extended their original stay by a few months. There’s really no substitute for all-inclusive furnished rentals and a co-living environment, with a furnished private room, that’s ready for you on day one.
‍

‍3) Increasing Value for the Local Property Industry:
We provide co-living communities for our guests by helping property owners draw more value from under-managed residential properties. We care about our customer community, of course, but we’re also excited about uniting property owners, vendors, and our team on one digital platform.
‍

‍4) Privacy Is the Priority:
There are no required social events. Our priority is providing privacy, a quiet environment, and security for all our guests. Our team will take care of cleaning the common spaces every week, so that our kitchen/dining areas are always comfortable. But if you want to expand your network or social circle, our office at WeWork offers you day/after-work communities. We just moved our headquarters to the newest WeWork offices in Long Island City, which is easily accessible by all subway lines.


‍5) 10 Years Perfecting the Co-Living Mindset:
Our founder started this business in his apartment after he couldn’t find appropriately priced accommodation for his first three months in New York. But our whole team has experienced co-living firsthand, so we understand what the customer feels and will need next. “We live and breathe co-living: first as roommates, and now serving our co-living guests.”
‍

‍6) A Sustainable Business Model in the Sharing Economy:
We won’t invest in luxury buildings like hotels or event spaces. We rent existing empty apartments and townhouses from the owners, put IKEA-type furniture in, and list the clean rooms on multiple digital platforms. We grow by our operational profit base, which comes from guests being charged fair prices and the revenue owners receive. However, what drives our growth is not the number of rooms, but our deep understanding of how to care for guests and rooms 24/7, and the intangible value within them.
‍

‍7) Our Vision - Making Dreams Come True:
CrossOver’s goal is to help our guests achieve their goals and dreams by providing the most affordable and flexible housing environment available. But it doesn’t stop here. Our guests’ dreams are expanding to a variety of locations around the globe, and CrossOver will be right there with them—powering the dreams of residents, landlords, and our staff in the wider world.

host_about:
Dear Airbnb guests!

Thanks for checking my profile. I manage furnished monthly rentals and co-living spaces in Manhattan, Queens, and Brooklyn with my team members. I have been managing furnished apartments for a decade and have had more than 5,600 guests from 90 countries so far. Please feel free to ask me any questions or requests!

*I can speak Japanese as well! Please feel free to contact me in Japanese.

Who we are: Our Principles

1) Growing Our Alumni Community:
We don’t require any extra/hidden fees to maximize our profits. Instead, our focus is on growing our alumni community. We believe that our services and fair pricing speak for themselves among our guests. Our alumni posted 700+ reviews from 2019 to 2021. What’s more, 80% of the reviews gave us five stars and 97% awarded more than four stars. Our alumni community spans the globe with 87 unique nationalities, and it has been expanding. We look forward to serving all our new guests: our alumni of tomorrow.
‍

‍2) Transparency. One All-Inclusive Price. That’s What We’re About:
There’s no math required. The price for our one-month minimum stay is simple and fair, no matter how long you stay with us. Our one-month price is already competitive (averaging $1,200 to $2,200, with 80% of our 150 rooms under $1,900 per month), compared to others’ discounted prices for three- to six-month stays. In 2020, 50%+ of our customers extended their original stay by a few months. There’s really no substitute for all-inclusive furnished rentals and a co-living environment, with a furnished private room, that’s ready for you on day one.
‍

‍3) Increasing Value for the Local Property Industry:
We provide co-living communities for our guests by helping property owners draw more value from under-managed residential properties. We care about our customer community, of course, but we’re also excited about uniting property owners, vendors, and our team on one digital platform.
‍

‍4) Privacy Is the Priority:
There are no required social events. Our priority is providing privacy, a quiet environment, and security for all our guests. Our team will take care of cleaning the common spaces every week, so that our kitchen/dining areas are always comfortable. But if you want to expand your network or social circle, our office at WeWork offers you day/after-work communities. We just moved our headquarters to the newest WeWork offices in Long Island City, which is easily accessible by all subway lines.


‍5) 10 Years Perfecting the Co-Living Mindset:
Our founder started this business in his apartment after he couldn’t find appropriately priced accommodation for his first three months in New York. But our whole team has experienced co-living firsthand, so we understand what the customer feels and will need next. “We live and breathe co-living: first as roommates, and now serving our co-living guests.”
‍

‍6) A Sustainable Business Model in the Sharing Economy:
We won’t invest in luxury buildings like hotels or event spaces. We rent existing empty apartments and townhouses from the owners, put IKEA-type furniture in, and list the clean rooms on multiple digital platforms. We grow by our operational profit base, which comes from guests being charged fair prices and the revenue owners receive. However, what drives our growth is not the number of rooms, but our deep understanding of how to care for guests and rooms 24/7, and the intangible value within them.
‍

‍7) Our Vision - Making Dreams Come True:
CrossOver’s goal is to help our guests achieve their goals and dreams by providing the most affordable and flexible housing environment available. But it doesn’t stop here. Our guests’ dreams are expanding to a variety of locations around the globe, and CrossOver will be right there with them—powering the dreams of residents, landlords, and our staff in the wider world.

host_about:
Dear Airbnb guests!

Thanks for checking my profile. I manage furnished monthly rentals and co-living spaces in Manhattan, Queens, and Brooklyn with my team members. I have been managing furnished apartments for a decade and have had more than 5,600 guests from 90 countries so far. Please feel free to ask me any questions or requests!

*I can speak Japanese as well! Please feel free to contact me in Japanese.

Who we are: Our Principles

1) Growing Our Alumni Community:
We don’t require any extra/hidden fees to maximize our profits. Instead, our focus is on growing our alumni community. We believe that our services and fair pricing speak for themselves among our guests. Our alumni posted 700+ reviews from 2019 to 2021. What’s more, 80% of the reviews gave us five stars and 97% awarded more than four stars. Our alumni community spans the globe with 87 unique nationalities, and it has been expanding. We look forward to serving all our new guests: our alumni of tomorrow.
‍

‍2) Transparency. One All-Inclusive Price. That’s What We’re About:
There’s no math required. The price for our one-month minimum stay is simple and fair, no matter how long you stay with us. Our one-month price is already competitive (averaging $1,200 to $2,200, with 80% of our 150 rooms under $1,900 per month), compared to others’ discounted prices for three- to six-month stays. In 2020, 50%+ of our customers extended their original stay by a few months. There’s really no substitute for all-inclusive furnished rentals and a co-living environment, with a furnished private room, that’s ready for you on day one.
‍

‍3) Increasing Value for the Local Property Industry:
We provide co-living communities for our guests by helping property owners draw more value from under-managed residential properties. We care about our customer community, of course, but we’re also excited about uniting property owners, vendors, and our team on one digital platform.
‍

‍4) Privacy Is the Priority:
There are no required social events. Our priority is providing privacy, a quiet environment, and security for all our guests. Our team will take care of cleaning the common spaces every week, so that our kitchen/dining areas are always comfortable. But if you want to expand your network or social circle, our office at WeWork offers you day/after-work communities. We just moved our headquarters to the newest WeWork offices in Long Island City, which is easily accessible by all subway lines.


‍5) 10 Years Perfecting the Co-Living Mindset:
Our founder started this business in his apartment after he couldn’t find appropriately priced accommodation for his first three months in New York. But our whole team has experienced co-living firsthand, so we understand what the customer feels and will need next. “We live and breathe co-living: first as roommates, and now serving our co-living guests.”
‍

‍6) A Sustainable Business Model in the Sharing Economy:
We won’t invest in luxury buildings like hotels or event spaces. We rent existing empty apartments and townhouses from the owners, put IKEA-type furniture in, and list the clean rooms on multiple digital platforms. We grow by our operational profit base, which comes from guests being charged fair prices and the revenue owners receive. However, what drives our growth is not the number of rooms, but our deep understanding of how to care for guests and rooms 24/7, and the intangible value within them.
‍

‍7) Our Vision - Making Dreams Come True:
CrossOver’s goal is to help our guests achieve their goals and dreams by providing the most affordable and flexible housing environment available. But it doesn’t stop here. Our guests’ dreams are expanding to a variety of locations around the globe, and CrossOver will be right there with them—powering the dreams of residents, landlords, and our staff in the wider world.

host_about:
Dear Airbnb guests!

Thanks for checking my profile. I manage furnished monthly rentals and co-living spaces in Manhattan, Queens, and Brooklyn with my team members. I have been managing furnished apartments for a decade and have had more than 5,600 guests from 90 countries so far. Please feel free to ask me any questions or requests!

*I can speak Japanese as well! Please feel free to contact me in Japanese.

Who we are: Our Principles

1) Growing Our Alumni Community:
We don’t require any extra/hidden fees to maximize our profits. Instead, our focus is on growing our alumni community. We believe that our services and fair pricing speak for themselves among our guests. Our alumni posted 700+ reviews from 2019 to 2021. What’s more, 80% of the reviews gave us five stars and 97% awarded more than four stars. Our alumni community spans the globe with 87 unique nationalities, and it has been expanding. We look forward to serving all our new guests: our alumni of tomorrow.
‍

‍2) Transparency. One All-Inclusive Price. That’s What We’re About:
There’s no math required. The price for our one-month minimum stay is simple and fair, no matter how long you stay with us. Our one-month price is already competitive (averaging $1,200 to $2,200, with 80% of our 150 rooms under $1,900 per month), compared to others’ discounted prices for three- to six-month stays. In 2020, 50%+ of our customers extended their original stay by a few months. There’s really no substitute for all-inclusive furnished rentals and a co-living environment, with a furnished private room, that’s ready for you on day one.
‍

‍3) Increasing Value for the Local Property Industry:
We provide co-living communities for our guests by helping property owners draw more value from under-managed residential properties. We care about our customer community, of course, but we’re also excited about uniting property owners, vendors, and our team on one digital platform.
‍

‍4) Privacy Is the Priority:
There are no required social events. Our priority is providing privacy, a quiet environment, and security for all our guests. Our team will take care of cleaning the common spaces every week, so that our kitchen/dining areas are always comfortable. But if you want to expand your network or social circle, our office at WeWork offers you day/after-work communities. We just moved our headquarters to the newest WeWork offices in Long Island City, which is easily accessible by all subway lines.


‍5) 10 Years Perfecting the Co-Living Mindset:
Our founder started this business in his apartment after he couldn’t find appropriately priced accommodation for his first three months in New York. But our whole team has experienced co-living firsthand, so we understand what the customer feels and will need next. “We live and breathe co-living: first as roommates, and now serving our co-living guests.”
‍

‍6) A Sustainable Business Model in the Sharing Economy:
We won’t invest in luxury buildings like hotels or event spaces. We rent existing empty apartments and townhouses from the owners, put IKEA-type furniture in, and list the clean rooms on multiple digital platforms. We grow by our operational profit base, which comes from guests being charged fair prices and the revenue owners receive. However, what drives our growth is not the number of rooms, but our deep understanding of how to care for guests and rooms 24/7, and the intangible value within them.
‍

‍7) Our Vision - Making Dreams Come True:
CrossOver’s goal is to help our guests achieve their goals and dreams by providing the most affordable and flexible housing environment available. But it doesn’t stop here. Our guests’ dreams are expanding to a variety of locations around the globe, and CrossOver will be right there with them—powering the dreams of residents, landlords, and our staff in the wider world.

neighborhood_overview:
Greenpoint is the northernmost neighborhood in the New York City borough of Brooklyn. Originally farmland, the residential core of Greenpoint was built on parcels divided during the 19th century, with rope factories and lumber yards lining the East River to the West, while the northeastern section along the Newtown Creek through East Williamsburg, became an industrial maritime reach.

Home to modern day Polish and Irish immigrants, Greenpoint is often referred to as Little Poland. With an easy commute from Manhattan via train or ferry, it is a quaint neighborhood full of chic bars, vintage cafes, and a mix of tasteful and timeless restaurants. Some of these renowned eateries include, ‘Oxomoco' (Mexican), ‘Sweet Chick’ (Southern Comfort) and ‘Lilia’ (Italian).

We grow by our operational profit base, which comes from guests being charged fair prices and the revenue owners receive. host_about:
Dear Airbnb guests!

Thanks for checking my profile. I manage furnished monthly rentals and co-living spaces in Manhattan, Queens, and Brooklyn with my team members. I have been managing furnished apartments for a decade and have had more than 5,600 guests from 90 countries so far. Please feel free to ask me any questions or requests!

*I can speak Japanese as well! Please feel free to contact me in Japanese.

Who we are: Our Principles

1) Growing Our Alumni Community:
We don’t require any extra/hidden fees to maximize our profits. Instead, our focus is on growing our alumni community. We believe that our services and fair pricing speak for themselves among our guests. Our alumni posted 700+ reviews from 2019 to 2021. What’s more, 80% of the reviews gave us five stars and 97% awarded more than four stars. Our alumni community spans the globe with 87 unique nationalities, and it has been expanding. We look forward to serving all our new guests: our alumni of tomorrow.
‍

‍2) Transparency. One All-Inclusive Price. That’s What We’re About:
There’s no math required. The price for our one-month minimum stay is simple and fair, no matter how long you stay with us. Our one-month price is already competitive (averaging $1,200 to $2,200, with 80% of our 150 rooms under $1,900 per month), compared to others’ discounted prices for three- to six-month stays. In 2020, 50%+ of our customers extended their original stay by a few months. There’s really no substitute for all-inclusive furnished rentals and a co-living environment, with a furnished private room, that’s ready for you on day one.
‍

‍3) Increasing Value for the Local Property Industry:
We provide co-living communities for our guests by helping property owners draw more value from under-managed residential properties. We care about our customer community, of course, but we’re also excited about uniting property owners, vendors, and our team on one digital platform.
‍

‍4) Privacy Is the Priority:
There are no required social events. Our priority is providing privacy, a quiet environment, and security for all our guests. Our team will take care of cleaning the common spaces every week, so that our kitchen/dining areas are always comfortable. But if you want to expand your network or social circle, our office at WeWork offers you day/after-work communities. We just moved our headquarters to the newest WeWork offices in Long Island City, which is easily accessible by all subway lines.


‍5) 10 Years Perfecting the Co-Living Mindset:
Our founder started this business in his apartment after he couldn’t find appropriately priced accommodation for his first three months in New York. But our whole team has experienced co-living firsthand, so we understand what the customer feels and will need next. “We live and breathe co-living: first as roommates, and now serving our co-living guests.”
‍

‍6) A Sustainable Business Model in the Sharing Economy:
We won’t invest in luxury buildings like hotels or event spaces. We rent existing empty apartments and townhouses from the owners, put IKEA-type furniture in, and list the clean rooms on multiple digital platforms. We grow by our operational profit base, which comes from guests being charged fair prices and the revenue owners receive. However, what drives our growth is not the number of rooms, but our deep understanding of how to care for guests and rooms 24/7, and the intangible value within them.
‍

‍7) Our Vision - Making Dreams Come True:
CrossOver’s goal is to help our guests achieve their goals and dreams by providing the most affordable and flexible housing environment available. But it doesn’t stop here. Our guests’ dreams are expanding to a variety of locations around the globe, and CrossOver will be right there with them—powering the dreams of residents, landlords, and our staff in the wider world.

host_about:
Dear Airbnb guests!

Thanks for checking my profile. I manage furnished monthly rentals and co-living spaces in Manhattan, Queens, and Brooklyn with my team members. I have been managing furnished apartments for a decade and have had more than 5,600 guests from 90 countries so far. Please feel free to ask me any questions or requests!

*I can speak Japanese as well! Please feel free to contact me in Japanese.

Who we are: Our Principles

1) Growing Our Alumni Community:
We don’t require any extra/hidden fees to maximize our profits. Instead, our focus is on growing our alumni community. We believe that our services and fair pricing speak for themselves among our guests. Our alumni posted 700+ reviews from 2019 to 2021. What’s more, 80% of the reviews gave us five stars and 97% awarded more than four stars. Our alumni community spans the globe with 87 unique nationalities, and it has been expanding. We look forward to serving all our new guests: our alumni of tomorrow.
‍

‍2) Transparency. One All-Inclusive Price. That’s What We’re About:
There’s no math required. The price for our one-month minimum stay is simple and fair, no matter how long you stay with us. Our one-month price is already competitive (averaging $1,200 to $2,200, with 80% of our 150 rooms under $1,900 per month), compared to others’ discounted prices for three- to six-month stays. In 2020, 50%+ of our customers extended their original stay by a few months. There’s really no substitute for all-inclusive furnished rentals and a co-living environment, with a furnished private room, that’s ready for you on day one.
‍

‍3) Increasing Value for the Local Property Industry:
We provide co-living communities for our guests by helping property owners draw more value from under-managed residential properties. We care about our customer community, of course, but we’re also excited about uniting property owners, vendors, and our team on one digital platform.
‍

‍4) Privacy Is the Priority:
There are no required social events. Our priority is providing privacy, a quiet environment, and security for all our guests. Our team will take care of cleaning the common spaces every week, so that our kitchen/dining areas are always comfortable. But if you want to expand your network or social circle, our office at WeWork offers you day/after-work communities. We just moved our headquarters to the newest WeWork offices in Long Island City, which is easily accessible by all subway lines.


‍5) 10 Years Perfecting the Co-Living Mindset:
Our founder started this business in his apartment after he couldn’t find appropriately priced accommodation for his first three months in New York. But our whole team has experienced co-living firsthand, so we understand what the customer feels and will need next. “We live and breathe co-living: first as roommates, and now serving our co-living guests.”
‍

‍6) A Sustainable Business Model in the Sharing Economy:
We won’t invest in luxury buildings like hotels or event spaces. We rent existing empty apartments and townhouses from the owners, put IKEA-type furniture in, and list the clean rooms on multiple digital platforms. We grow by our operational profit base, which comes from guests being charged fair prices and the revenue owners receive. However, what drives our growth is not the number of rooms, but our deep understanding of how to care for guests and rooms 24/7, and the intangible value within them.
‍

‍7) Our Vision - Making Dreams Come True:
CrossOver’s goal is to help our guests achieve their goals and dreams by providing the most affordable and flexible housing environment available. But it doesn’t stop here. Our guests’ dreams are expanding to a variety of locations around the globe, and CrossOver will be right there with them—powering the dreams of residents, landlords, and our staff in the wider world.

neighborhood_overview:
Of Brooklyn’s gentrifying neighborhoods, few have seen such rapid change as Bushwick. The neighborhood has grown as a natural extension of Williamsburg—a haven for creatives and young folks looking for lower rents. But well before its trendy vibe put it on the map, Bushwick was a forested enclave originally settled by the Dutch—its name is derived from a Dutch word “Boswijck,”defined as “little town in the woods”—and later, German immigrants who began building breweries and factories.

host_about:
Dear Airbnb guests!

Thanks for checking my profile. I manage furnished monthly rentals and co-living spaces in Manhattan, Queens, and Brooklyn with my team members. I have been managing furnished apartments for a decade and have had more than 5,600 guests from 90 countries so far. Please feel free to ask me any questions or requests!

*I can speak Japanese as well! Please feel free to contact me in Japanese.

Who we are: Our Principles

1) Growing Our Alumni Community:
We don’t require any extra/hidden fees to maximize our profits. Instead, our focus is on growing our alumni community. We believe that our services and fair pricing speak for themselves among our guests. Our alumni posted 700+ reviews from 2019 to 2021. What’s more, 80% of the reviews gave us five stars and 97% awarded more than four stars. Our alumni community spans the globe with 87 unique nationalities, and it has been expanding. We look forward to serving all our new guests: our alumni of tomorrow.
‍

‍2) Transparency. One All-Inclusive Price. That’s What We’re About:
There’s no math required. The price for our one-month minimum stay is simple and fair, no matter how long you stay with us. Our one-month price is already competitive (averaging $1,200 to $2,200, with 80% of our 150 rooms under $1,900 per month), compared to others’ discounted prices for three- to six-month stays. In 2020, 50%+ of our customers extended their original stay by a few months. There’s really no substitute for all-inclusive furnished rentals and a co-living environment, with a furnished private room, that’s ready for you on day one.
‍

‍3) Increasing Value for the Local Property Industry:
We provide co-living communities for our guests by helping property owners draw more value from under-managed residential properties. We care about our customer community, of course, but we’re also excited about uniting property owners, vendors, and our team on one digital platform.
‍

‍4) Privacy Is the Priority:
There are no required social events. Our priority is providing privacy, a quiet environment, and security for all our guests. Our team will take care of cleaning the common spaces every week, so that our kitchen/dining areas are always comfortable. But if you want to expand your network or social circle, our office at WeWork offers you day/after-work communities. We just moved our headquarters to the newest WeWork offices in Long Island City, which is easily accessible by all subway lines.


‍5) 10 Years Perfecting the Co-Living Mindset:
Our founder started this business in his apartment after he couldn’t find appropriately priced accommodation for his first three months in New York. But our whole team has experienced co-living firsthand, so we understand what the customer feels and will need next. “We live and breathe co-living: first as roommates, and now serving our co-living guests.”
‍

‍6) A Sustainable Business Model in the Sharing Economy:
We won’t invest in luxury buildings like hotels or event spaces. We rent existing empty apartments and townhouses from the owners, put IKEA-type furniture in, and list the clean rooms on multiple digital platforms. We grow by our operational profit base, which comes from guests being charged fair prices and the revenue owners receive. However, what drives our growth is not the number of rooms, but our deep understanding of how to care for guests and rooms 24/7, and the intangible value within them.
‍

‍7) Our Vision - Making Dreams Come True:
CrossOver’s goal is to help our guests achieve their goals and dreams by providing the most affordable and flexible housing environment available. But it doesn’t stop here. Our guests’ dreams are expanding to a variety of locations around the globe, and CrossOver will be right there with them—powering the dreams of residents, landlords, and our staff in the wider world.

host_about:
Dear Airbnb guests!

Thanks for checking my profile. I manage furnished monthly rentals and co-living spaces in Manhattan, Queens, and Brooklyn with my team members. I have been managing furnished apartments for a decade and have had more than 5,600 guests from 90 countries so far. Please feel free to ask me any questions or requests!

*I can speak Japanese as well! Please feel free to contact me in Japanese.

Who we are: Our Principles

1) Growing Our Alumni Community:
We don’t require any extra/hidden fees to maximize our profits. Instead, our focus is on growing our alumni community. We believe that our services and fair pricing speak for themselves among our guests. Our alumni posted 700+ reviews from 2019 to 2021. What’s more, 80% of the reviews gave us five stars and 97% awarded more than four stars. Our alumni community spans the globe with 87 unique nationalities, and it has been expanding. We look forward to serving all our new guests: our alumni of tomorrow.
‍

‍2) Transparency. One All-Inclusive Price. That’s What We’re About:
There’s no math required. The price for our one-month minimum stay is simple and fair, no matter how long you stay with us. Our one-month price is already competitive (averaging $1,200 to $2,200, with 80% of our 150 rooms under $1,900 per month), compared to others’ discounted prices for three- to six-month stays. In 2020, 50%+ of our customers extended their original stay by a few months. There’s really no substitute for all-inclusive furnished rentals and a co-living environment, with a furnished private room, that’s ready for you on day one.
‍

‍3) Increasing Value for the Local Property Industry:
We provide co-living communities for our guests by helping property owners draw more value from under-managed residential properties. We care about our customer community, of course, but we’re also excited about uniting property owners, vendors, and our team on one digital platform.
‍

‍4) Privacy Is the Priority:
There are no required social events. Our priority is providing privacy, a quiet environment, and security for all our guests. Our team will take care of cleaning the common spaces every week, so that our kitchen/dining areas are always comfortable. But if you want to expand your network or social circle, our office at WeWork offers you day/after-work communities. We just moved our headquarters to the newest WeWork offices in Long Island City, which is easily accessible by all subway lines.


‍5) 10 Years Perfecting the Co-Living Mindset:
Our founder started this business in his apartment after he couldn’t find appropriately priced accommodation for his first three months in New York. But our whole team has experienced co-living firsthand, so we understand what the customer feels and will need next. “We live and breathe co-living: first as roommates, and now serving our co-living guests.”
‍

‍6) A Sustainable Business Model in the Sharing Economy:
We won’t invest in luxury buildings like hotels or event spaces. We rent existing empty apartments and townhouses from the owners, put IKEA-type furniture in, and list the clean rooms on multiple digital platforms. We grow by our operational profit base, which comes from guests being charged fair prices and the revenue owners receive. However, what drives our growth is not the number of rooms, but our deep understanding of how to care for guests and rooms 24/7, and the intangible value within them.
‍

‍7) Our Vision - Making Dreams Come True:
CrossOver’s goal is to help our guests achieve their goals and dreams by providing the most affordable and flexible housing environment available. But it doesn’t stop here. Our guests’ dreams are expanding to a variety of locations around the globe, and CrossOver will be right there with them—powering the dreams of residents, landlords, and our staff in the wider world.

Dear Airbnb guests!

Thanks for checking my profile. I manage furnished monthly rentals and co-living spaces in Manhattan, Queens, and Brooklyn with my team members. I have been managing furnished apartments for a decade and have had more than 5,600 guests from 90 countries so far. Please feel free to ask me any questions or requests!

Who we are: Our Principles

1) Growing Our Alumni Community:
We don’t require any extra/hidden fees to maximize our profits. Instead, our focus is on growing our alumni community. We believe that our services and fair pricing speak for themselves among our guests. Our alumni posted 700+ reviews from 2019 to 2021. What’s more, 80% of the reviews gave us five stars and 97% awarded more than four stars. Our alumni community spans the globe with 87 unique nationalities, and it has been expanding. We look forward to serving all our new guests: our alumni of tomorrow.
‍

‍2) Transparency. One All-Inclusive Price. That’s What We’re About:
There’s no math required. The price for our one-month minimum stay is simple and fair, no matter how long you stay with us. Our one-month price is already competitive (averaging $1,200 to $2,200, with 80% of our 150 rooms under $1,900 per month), compared to others’ discounted prices for three- to six-month stays. In 2020, 50%+ of our customers extended their original stay by a few months. There’s really no substitute for all-inclusive furnished rentals and a co-living environment, with a furnished private room, that’s ready for you on day one.
‍

‍3) Increasing Value for the Local Property Industry:
We provide co-living communities for our guests by helping property owners draw more value from under-managed residential properties. We care about our customer community, of course, but we’re also excited about uniting property owners, vendors, and our team on one digital platform.
‍

‍4) Privacy Is the Priority:
There are no required social events. Our priority is providing privacy, a quiet environment, and security for all our guests. Our team will take care of cleaning the common spaces every week, so that our kitchen/dining areas are always comfortable. But if you want to expand your network or social circle, our office at WeWork offers you day/after-work communities. We just moved our headquarters to the newest WeWork offices in Long Island City, which is easily accessible by all subway lines.


‍5) 10 Years Perfecting the Co-Living Mindset:
Our founder started this business in his apartment after he couldn’t find appropriately priced accommodation for his first three months in New York. But our whole team has experienced co-living firsthand, so we understand what the customer feels and will need next. “We live and breathe co-living: first as roommates, and now serving our co-living guests.”
‍

‍6) A Sustainable Business Model in the Sharing Economy:
We won’t invest in luxury buildings like hotels or event spaces. We rent existing empty apartments and townhouses from the owners, put IKEA-type furniture in, and list the clean rooms on multiple digital platforms. We grow by our operational profit base, which comes from guests being charged fair prices and the revenue owners receive. However, what drives our growth is not the number of rooms, but our deep understanding of how to care for guests and rooms 24/7, and the intangible value within them.
‍

‍7) Our Vision - Making Dreams Come True:
CrossOver’s goal is to help our guests achieve their goals and dreams by providing the most affordable and flexible housing environment available. But it doesn’t stop here. Our guests’ dreams are expanding to a variety of locations around the globe, and CrossOver will be right there with them—powering the dreams of residents, landlords, and our staff in the wider world.

host_about:
Dear Airbnb guests!

Thanks for checking my profile. I manage furnished monthly rentals and co-living spaces in Manhattan, Queens, and Brooklyn with my team members. I have been managing furnished apartments for a decade and have had more than 5,600 guests from 90 countries so far. Please feel free to ask me any questions or requests!

*I can speak Japanese as well! Please feel free to contact me in Japanese.

Who we are: Our Principles

1) Growing Our Alumni Community:
We don’t require any extra/hidden fees to maximize our profits. Instead, our focus is on growing our alumni community. We believe that our services and fair pricing speak for themselves among our guests. Our alumni posted 700+ reviews from 2019 to 2021. What’s more, 80% of the reviews gave us five stars and 97% awarded more than four stars. Our alumni community spans the globe with 87 unique nationalities, and it has been expanding. We look forward to serving all our new guests: our alumni of tomorrow.
‍

‍2) Transparency. One All-Inclusive Price. That’s What We’re About:
There’s no math required. The price for our one-month minimum stay is simple and fair, no matter how long you stay with us. Our one-month price is already competitive (averaging $1,200 to $2,200, with 80% of our 150 rooms under $1,900 per month), compared to others’ discounted prices for three- to six-month stays. In 2020, 50%+ of our customers extended their original stay by a few months. There’s really no substitute for all-inclusive furnished rentals and a co-living environment, with a furnished private room, that’s ready for you on day one.
‍

‍3) Increasing Value for the Local Property Industry:
We provide co-living communities for our guests by helping property owners draw more value from under-managed residential properties. We care about our customer community, of course, but we’re also excited about uniting property owners, vendors, and our team on one digital platform.
‍

‍4) Privacy Is the Priority:
There are no required social events. Our priority is providing privacy, a quiet environment, and security for all our guests. Our team will take care of cleaning the common spaces every week, so that our kitchen/dining areas are always comfortable. But if you want to expand your network or social circle, our office at WeWork offers you day/after-work communities. We just moved our headquarters to the newest WeWork offices in Long Island City, which is easily accessible by all subway lines.


‍5) 10 Years Perfecting the Co-Living Mindset:
Our founder started this business in his apartment after he couldn’t find appropriately priced accommodation for his first three months in New York. But our whole team has experienced co-living firsthand, so we understand what the customer feels and will need next. “We live and breathe co-living: first as roommates, and now serving our co-living guests.”
‍

‍6) A Sustainable Business Model in the Sharing Economy:
We won’t invest in luxury buildings like hotels or event spaces. We rent existing empty apartments and townhouses from the owners, put IKEA-type furniture in, and list the clean rooms on multiple digital platforms. We grow by our operational profit base, which comes from guests being charged fair prices and the revenue owners receive. However, what drives our growth is not the number of rooms, but our deep understanding of how to care for guests and rooms 24/7, and the intangible value within them.
‍

‍7) Our Vision - Making Dreams Come True:
CrossOver’s goal is to help our guests achieve their goals and dreams by providing the most affordable and flexible housing environment available. But it doesn’t stop here. Our guests’ dreams are expanding to a variety of locations around the globe, and CrossOver will be right there with them—powering the dreams of residents, landlords, and our staff in the wider world.

host_about:
Dear Airbnb guests!

Thanks for checking my profile. I manage furnished monthly rentals and co-living spaces in Manhattan, Queens, and Brooklyn with my team members. I have been managing furnished apartments for a decade and have had more than 5,600 guests from 90 countries so far. Please feel free to ask me any questions or requests!

*I can speak Japanese as well! Please feel free to contact me in Japanese.

Who we are: Our Principles

1) Growing Our Alumni Community:
We don’t require any extra/hidden fees to maximize our profits. Instead, our focus is on growing our alumni community. We believe that our services and fair pricing speak for themselves among our guests. Our alumni posted 700+ reviews from 2019 to 2021. What’s more, 80% of the reviews gave us five stars and 97% awarded more than four stars. Our alumni community spans the globe with 87 unique nationalities, and it has been expanding. We look forward to serving all our new guests: our alumni of tomorrow.
‍

‍2) Transparency. One All-Inclusive Price. That’s What We’re About:
There’s no math required. The price for our one-month minimum stay is simple and fair, no matter how long you stay with us. Our one-month price is already competitive (averaging $1,200 to $2,200, with 80% of our 150 rooms under $1,900 per month), compared to others’ discounted prices for three- to six-month stays. In 2020, 50%+ of our customers extended their original stay by a few months. There’s really no substitute for all-inclusive furnished rentals and a co-living environment, with a furnished private room, that’s ready for you on day one.
‍

‍3) Increasing Value for the Local Property Industry:
We provide co-living communities for our guests by helping property owners draw more value from under-managed residential properties. We care about our customer community, of course, but we’re also excited about uniting property owners, vendors, and our team on one digital platform.
‍

‍4) Privacy Is the Priority:
There are no required social events. Our priority is providing privacy, a quiet environment, and security for all our guests. Our team will take care of cleaning the common spaces every week, so that our kitchen/dining areas are always comfortable. But if you want to expand your network or social circle, our office at WeWork offers you day/after-work communities. We just moved our headquarters to the newest WeWork offices in Long Island City, which is easily accessible by all subway lines.


‍5) 10 Years Perfecting the Co-Living Mindset:
Our founder started this business in his apartment after he couldn’t find appropriately priced accommodation for his first three months in New York. But our whole team has experienced co-living firsthand, so we understand what the customer feels and will need next. “We live and breathe co-living: first as roommates, and now serving our co-living guests.”
‍

‍6) A Sustainable Business Model in the Sharing Economy:
We won’t invest in luxury buildings like hotels or event spaces. We rent existing empty apartments and townhouses from the owners, put IKEA-type furniture in, and list the clean rooms on multiple digital platforms. We grow by our operational profit base, which comes from guests being charged fair prices and the revenue owners receive. However, what drives our growth is not the number of rooms, but our deep understanding of how to care for guests and rooms 24/7, and the intangible value within them.
‍

‍7) Our Vision - Making Dreams Come True:
CrossOver’s goal is to help our guests achieve their goals and dreams by providing the most affordable and flexible housing environment available. But it doesn’t stop here. Our guests’ dreams are expanding to a variety of locations around the globe, and CrossOver will be right there with them—powering the dreams of residents, landlords, and our staff in the wider world.

host_about:
Dear Airbnb guests!

Thanks for checking my profile. I manage furnished monthly rentals and co-living spaces in Manhattan, Queens, and Brooklyn with my team members. I have been managing furnished apartments for a decade and have had more than 5,600 guests from 90 countries so far. Please feel free to ask me any questions or requests!

*I can speak Japanese as well! Please feel free to contact me in Japanese.

Who we are: Our Principles

1) Growing Our Alumni Community:
We don’t require any extra/hidden fees to maximize our profits. Instead, our focus is on growing our alumni community. We believe that our services and fair pricing speak for themselves among our guests. Our alumni posted 700+ reviews from 2019 to 2021. What’s more, 80% of the reviews gave us five stars and 97% awarded more than four stars. Our alumni community spans the globe with 87 unique nationalities, and it has been expanding. We look forward to serving all our new guests: our alumni of tomorrow.
‍

‍2) Transparency. One All-Inclusive Price. That’s What We’re About:
There’s no math required. The price for our one-month minimum stay is simple and fair, no matter how long you stay with us. Our one-month price is already competitive (averaging $1,200 to $2,200, with 80% of our 150 rooms under $1,900 per month), compared to others’ discounted prices for three- to six-month stays. In 2020, 50%+ of our customers extended their original stay by a few months. There’s really no substitute for all-inclusive furnished rentals and a co-living environment, with a furnished private room, that’s ready for you on day one.
‍

‍3) Increasing Value for the Local Property Industry:
We provide co-living communities for our guests by helping property owners draw more value from under-managed residential properties. We care about our customer community, of course, but we’re also excited about uniting property owners, vendors, and our team on one digital platform.
‍

‍4) Privacy Is the Priority:
There are no required social events. Our priority is providing privacy, a quiet environment, and security for all our guests. Our team will take care of cleaning the common spaces every week, so that our kitchen/dining areas are always comfortable. But if you want to expand your network or social circle, our office at WeWork offers you day/after-work communities. We just moved our headquarters to the newest WeWork offices in Long Island City, which is easily accessible by all subway lines.


‍5) 10 Years Perfecting the Co-Living Mindset:
Our founder started this business in his apartment after he couldn’t find appropriately priced accommodation for his first three months in New York. But our whole team has experienced co-living firsthand, so we understand what the customer feels and will need next. “We live and breathe co-living: first as roommates, and now serving our co-living guests.”
‍

‍6) A Sustainable Business Model in the Sharing Economy:
We won’t invest in luxury buildings like hotels or event spaces. We rent existing empty apartments and townhouses from the owners, put IKEA-type furniture in, and list the clean rooms on multiple digital platforms. We grow by our operational profit base, which comes from guests being charged fair prices and the revenue owners receive. However, what drives our growth is not the number of rooms, but our deep understanding of how to care for guests and rooms 24/7, and the intangible value within them.
‍

‍7) Our Vision - Making Dreams Come True:
CrossOver’s goal is to help our guests achieve their goals and dreams by providing the most affordable and flexible housing environment available. But it doesn’t stop here. Our guests’ dreams are expanding to a variety of locations around the globe, and CrossOver will be right there with them—powering the dreams of residents, landlords, and our staff in the wider world.

name: Beautiful Loft Suite in Brooklyn
description:
Loft Suite @ Henry Norman Hotel

Located in Greenpoint, Brooklyn and housed in a converted 19th-century warehouse, the Henry Norman Hotel features modern lofts and suites with hardwood floors, antiques and contemporary art.

Our hotel interiors are adorned with vintage furnishings, found objects, and bespoke works by local artists. Guests are also privy to outdoor terraces, available for alfresco lounging, as well as a cozy indoor living room space located on the ground floor of the property.
neighborhood_overview:
Greenpoint is the northernmost neighborhood in the New York City borough of Brooklyn. Originally farmland, the residential core of Greenpoint was built on parcels divided during the 19th century, with rope factories and lumber yards lining the East River to the West, while the northeastern section along the Newtown Creek through East Williamsburg, became an industrial maritime reach.

Home to modern day Polish and Irish immigrants, Greenpoint is often referred to as Little Poland. With an easy commute from Manhattan via train or ferry, it is a quaint neighborhood full of chic bars, vintage cafes, and a mix of tasteful and timeless restaurants. Some of these renowned eateries include, ‘Oxomoco' (Mexican), ‘Sweet Chick’ (Southern Comfort) and ‘Lilia’ (Italian).
